Global regular differences

Exposition, proofs and exercises: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. CC0.

A local derivative-growth function need not extend to the whole real space. It does, however, have a global representative up to an analytic function near any chosen point. A Gaussian reconstruction gives this representative by restricting the Gaussian centers to a small ball. No derivative falls on that restriction. The part with centers outside the ball is analytic near the point.

This construction gives the global intersection formula for derivative-growth wavefront sets, including the growth classes which do not admit compactly supported cutoffs.

Proposition 7 (finitely many prescribed germs). At finitely many distinct points , prescribe germs . There is a single such that is analytic near each .

Proof. Choose balls with pairwise disjoint closures, each containing its point and lying in the domain of a representative . This is possible by taking radii smaller than one third of every pairwise distance and then shrinking into the respective domains. Theorem 5 gives , with analytic at and analytic outside . For , all terms with index different from are analytic near . Finite sums preserve by its defining bounds. This proves the assertion.

Exercise 5 (intermediate: genuine extension versus analytic difference). On , take . Prove that it has no real-analytic extension to all of , and explain why Theorem 5 is consistent with this.

Solution. A real-analytic extension would make analytic on and zero on . The set of points where every derivative of is zero is closed by continuity, nonempty because it contains , and open by the convergent Taylor expansion. Connectedness of the line forces that set to be all of . Evaluation at would then give . On the other hand, is a global analytic function and is analytic on . The theorem requires an analytic difference near the chosen point, rather than equality there.
